answer: Anchor each epoch's full identity set as a Merkle root posted to an external settlement chain, so the honest record hangs on an immutable trellis of timestamped commitments no local node can quietly rewrite. To slip in a backdated clone an attacker must buy a fresh external re-anchor that the next honest commitment overwrites — a lotus that blooms for one block then is gone. Every thread of forged history costs real outside gas per fake: 1000 clones means 1000 separately paid re-anchors, strictly linear and none recoverable, so cheap duplication never amortizes.
